blocks.content: Introduction to Maintenance vs preventive maintenance (recognition)
Recognize maintenance and preventive maintenance concepts at CAET entry level.

items.definition: Per FAA regulations: inspection, overhaul, repair, preservation, and replacement of parts — explicitly excluding preventive maintenance, which is a separate regulatory category.
items.analogy: Like a car service package covering inspections and repairs — but not the DIY tasks the owner is allowed to perform themselves.

items.definition: Under 14 CFR Part 43, preventive maintenance is limited to certificated pilots on aircraft they own or operate — restricted to simple tasks explicitly listed in Part 43 Appendix A.
items.analogy: Like a homeowner being allowed to replace their own light switches but not wire a subpanel — a defined, limited scope for non-professionals on their own property.

blocks.question: According to FAA regulations, which activity is explicitly EXCLUDED from the definition of 'maintenance'?
blocks.feedback: The FAA definition of maintenance lists inspection, overhaul, repair, preservation, and replacement of parts. Preventive maintenance is carved out as a separate category that certificated pilots may perform on aircraft they own or operate.

blocks.question: Why is preventive maintenance under Part 43 limited to certificated pilots on aircraft they own or operate?
choices: Because pilots receive basic maintenance training and can perform any simple task
Because Part 43 restricts all maintenance to aircraft owners regardless of certification level
Because it covers only simple tasks not requiring mechanic training, on the owner's aircraft only
Because the FAA determined pilots are more reliable than mechanics for owner-performed tasks
blocks.feedback: Preventive maintenance covers simple tasks (oil changes, tire replacement, bulb changes) that don't require mechanic-level training. The owner/operator limitation ensures the person has a direct stake in the aircraft's airworthiness. Performing preventive maintenance on someone else's aircraft is not authorized.
